title: Carroll cabinet to fix business links
full_text:
Victorian Premier Ben Carroll has scrapped the infrastructure and Suburban Rail Loop portfolios from his new frontbench and appointed a new treasurer who vowed to immediately meet with employers to begin repairing Labor's relationship with business.
Carroll's revamped cabinet was sworn in at Government House on Tuesday morning, with key allies promoted and loyalists to former leader Jacinta Allan demoted in a widespread reshuffle the premier said would take Labor in a "new direction".
Deputy Premier Gabrielle Williams has been appointed education minister, where she will need to end the long-running pay dispute with teachers. As deputy, she was able to nominate her own portfolio, and has also picked up skills and training, First Peoples, and women and gender equality.
Colin Brooks has been promoted to the Treasury and industrial relations portfolios, Anthony Carbines will move from police and take on the newly created roles of artificial intelligence and the digital economy, and Jaclyn Symes will take on energy and resources.
The ministry was cut from 22 positions to 20 in a move Carroll said was aimed at "saving money" but Labor sources attributed to internal factions.
The biggest shift from Carroll's predecessors Allan and Daniel Andrews was to abolish the SRL and infrastructure portfolios, which have become synonymous with corruption and criminality and led to Allan's downfall. "We are running a smaller government, a more efficient and more effective government where it extracts the best value for taxpayers," Carroll said.
"I've considered this very carefully. Whether it's the public transport minister being in charge of both infrastructure and services, versus the roads minister being in charge of both roads and infrastructure."
Allan ally Symes was demoted from Treasury, Steve Dimopoulos lost his major events portfolio, and Sonya Kilkenny was moved out of finance but retained attorney-general and planning as part of a deal she struck to withdraw her leadership nomination.
Lizzie Blandthorn remains children and disability minister, Enver Erdogan was promoted to finance, and Ingrid Stitt was appointed health minister.
Paul Edbrooke picked up police and emergency services. The new police minister, who only joined the frontbench in April, said he supported keeping police stations open. Victoria Police has cut counter opening hours at 40 stations due to resourcing challenges.
Luba Grigorovitch, part of the cross-factional delegation who visited Allan last week to say she had lost the support of caucus, was not rewarded. Tim Richardson, elevated to cabinet as part of the Kilkenny deal, will take on local government and consumer affairs.
Vicki Ward will become the new public transport minister, giving her responsibility for the SRL. Nina Taylor has been appointed cabinet secretary.
Following the swearing-in ceremony, Brooks said his parents were small business owners and one of the first things he would do as treasurer was reach out to industry groups and businesses.
"I think rebuilding a relationship with business is a key part of that agenda," Brooks said. "I'll be meeting with businesses to understand at an even greater level what some of their concerns are and how we can grow jobs for Victorians further.
"Small business, big business provide jobs for thousands of Victorians, so we need to work with them very closely."
His comments are in sharp contrast to Allan, who had increasingly picked fights with businesses to win electoral support.
Brooks, who is well respected in the business community, said he would be focused on "respecting every taxpayer dollar" and would seek briefings from treasury on fiscal management, with net debt forecast to climb to about $200 billion in four years.
Opposition Leader Jess Wilson said Carroll was "shuffling the deck chairs on the Titanic" just months out from the November state election.
"The same faces that have been around the cabinet table for years, endorsing decisions by Daniel Andrews and Jacinta Allan, and the same corrupt Labor government," Wilson said. "Ben Carroll may want to eliminate the term Big Build and the ministers responsible, but the corruption is still running rife on these sites."
